title: LEARN: A Story-Driven Layout-to-Image Generation Framework for STEM Instruction
extended_summary:
This paper addresses the problem of generating pedagogically useful visuals for STEM instruction using generative AI. The authors argue that existing text-to-image and layout-to-image systems are not well suited to education because they lack narrative continuity, spatial precision, and explicit alignment with instructional theories such as Cognitive Load Theory and Bloom’s taxonomy. The paper asks whether a layout-aware, story-driven image generation framework can produce more coherent and educationally aligned STEM illustrations.

The proposed intervention is LEARN, a layout-conditioned diffusion framework that converts STEM concept prompts into structured visual layouts and then into generated images. It is trained using a curated and enriched BookCover dataset derived from a public book cover corpus, with added bounding boxes and semantic annotations created using CLIPSeg, SAM, and GPT-4o. The framework combines narrative encoding, a transformer-based layout generator, layout-to-image diffusion synthesis, contrastive visual-semantic alignment, and prompt modulation to improve spatial coherence, semantic consistency, and narrative flow in generated educational visuals.

The empirical context includes technical evaluations on RC-COCO and human evaluation of 50 STEM prompts rendered by LEARN, GLIGEN, and textbook figures. The user study involved 12 educators and 26 students aged 11–22, which maps to middle school, high school, and undergraduate populations. The acknowledgments mention participation organized through No.1 Senior Middle School of Shouguang, and the authors are affiliated with institutions in Japan and China, though the participant location is most directly tied to China. The study appears to involve both quantitative model benchmarking and human ratings of clarity, cognitive load, narrative flow, and concept alignment.

The main conclusions are that LEARN improves structural fidelity and educational usefulness relative to comparison systems. In benchmark experiments, it achieved the best FID and strong region-level alignment metrics after fine-tuning on the BookCover corpus. In the human study, LEARN outputs were rated 23% higher in clarity and 31% lower in perceived cognitive load, and 96% of participants reported stronger narrative flow and better concept alignment. The authors conclude that LEARN shows promise as a practical generative AI tool for STEM instruction, while also acknowledging limitations related to concept decomposition, classroom usability, and integration with more dynamic multimodal educational systems.

identified_tools.name: LEARN
identified_tools.description: A layout-aware diffusion framework for generating story-driven, pedagogically aligned STEM illustrations from concept prompts using structured layouts, semantic alignment, and a curated BookCover dataset.
identified_tools.use_case: Studied as a generative visual content system for STEM instruction that creates layout-guided, multi-frame illustrations intended to support conceptual progression, reduce cognitive load, and improve instructional clarity.

findings.finding_summary: On the RC-COCO benchmark after fine-tuning on the BookCover corpus, LEARN achieved FID=27.16, CropCLIP=27.92, and SAMIoU=81.52. Compared with ablations, removing layout embeddings worsened performance to FID=36.45, CropCLIP=24.63, and SAMIoU=76.36; removing alignment losses also reduced semantic and spatial quality.
findings.measure: RC-COCO image generation metrics: Fréchet Inception Distance (FID), CropCLIP Score, SAMIoU

findings.finding_summary: Against fine-tuned rich-context layout-to-image baselines, LEARN had the best FID at 27.16 versus GLIGEN's 27.95 and SDXL (Rich-Context)'s 27.41, while showing competitive but not best layout metrics. LEARN scored CropCLIP=27.92 and SAMIoU=81.52, compared with SDXL's CropCLIP=28.15 and SAMIoU=80.87.
findings.measure: Comparative RC-COCO generation metrics versus GLIGEN and SDXL (Rich-Context): FID, CropCLIP, SAMIoU

findings.finding_summary: In a human study, 12 educators and 26 students evaluated 50 STEM prompts rendered by LEARN, GLIGEN, and textbook figures on a 5-point Likert scale. LEARN's outputs scored 23% higher in clarity, reduced perceived cognitive load by 31%, and 96% of participants reported stronger narrative flow and improved concept alignment.
findings.measure: Human ratings of clarity, perceived cognitive load, narrative flow, and concept alignment on 50 STEM prompts using a 5-point Likert scale
findings.effect_size: 23% higher clarity; 31% lower perceived cognitive load; 96% reported stronger narrative flow and improved concept alignment

quality_tier_rationale: The paper reports benchmark experiments plus a small human study with educators and students, but it does not present an RCT or strong quasi-experimental design on student learning outcomes. Most evidence is model-evaluation and perception-based rather than causal educational impact evidence.
impact_tier_rationale: Reported human-study improvements are directionally positive and practically meaningful (23% higher clarity, 31% lower perceived cognitive load), but impacts are based on a small sample and non-standardized outcome measures rather than robust achievement effects.
